summary.text: Franklin Foil is a Republican member of the Louisiana State Senate representing District 16, which the legislature's member page lists as covering East Baton Rouge Parish. First elected in 2019, Franklin Foil chairs the Revenue and Fiscal Affairs Committee and sits on the Insurance and Local and Municipal Affairs committees.

paragraphs.text: Franklin Foil's Senate biography says he is a native of Baton Rouge who graduated from University High School and Louisiana State University, then from Loyola School of Law in New Orleans.
It says he was commissioned as an officer in the U.S. Navy JAG Corps, spent four years on active duty, and then returned to Baton Rouge to start a private law practice.

The biography says he served on active duty and in the Navy Reserves for 30 years, retiring as a Navy Captain who served as an appellate court judge in Washington, DC, and that he was awarded the Legion of Merit.
It says he was elected to Senate District 16 in 2019 after 12 years as the representative for House District 70.

The biography lists him as active in the American Legion, the Rotary Club of Baton Rouge, and the LSU Cadets of the Ole War Skule, and says he is a member of First Presbyterian Church in Baton Rouge, where he has served as an Elder.
The Senate page lists Franklin Foil's education as a B.A. in political science from Louisiana State University (1987) and a J.D. from Loyola School of Law (1991).

The Senate page lists Franklin Foil's committee assignments as Revenue and Fiscal Affairs (chair), Insurance, Local and Municipal Affairs, Finance (ex officio), Joint Legislative Committee on Capital Outlay, Joint Legislative Committee on the Budget, State Bond Commission, Select Committee on Military and Veterans Affairs, and Senate Select Committee on Homeland Security, and caucus and delegation affiliations as Capital Region Legislative Delegation and Louisiana Republican Legislative Delegation.
